reuse.why: Every weekend/holiday decision goes through the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend helper (now backed by one isWeekendOrHoliday), and the new range handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule/RSchedule like getUpcomingDates.

duplication.why: The `skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend(date, mode, frequency, holidays) : date` wrapper is repeated in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and a new schedule-template wrapper, and getDatesInRange restates getUpcomingDates' build-schedule/map/try-captureBreadcrumb skeleton.

placement.why: Weekend, holiday and window logic sits in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in server/schedules/app.ts alongside get-upcoming-dates, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Changes stay on the four requests; the RecurConfig and parseRecurDate edits are needed to carry the new fields.

maintainability.why: The core rule is central, but whether weekend handling applies is still decided at each caller, and getUpcomingDates encodes the daily-skip rule again in its own over-fetch (count*7), so a maintainer must keep several sites in step.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates computes `config.skipWeekend && config.frequency === 'daily'` itself to size the over-fetch, re-deciding the daily-skip rule outside getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange is getUpcomingDates reshaped (range instead of take, Set instead of slice), and schedule-template's getWeekendAdjustedDay is the same skipWeekend ternary renamed into a local helper.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained `frequency` and `holidays` parameters and a `frequency === 'daily' -> null` branch; getUpcomingDates separately re-checks the daily rule for its lookahead.
